merged_guidance.visa_category: Visa-free entry for short business visits
merged_guidance.permitted_stay: Up to 30 days per stay under the bilateral agreement, and no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. The unilateral scheme allows up to 60 days for business engagements
merged_guidance.passport_validity: Valid at least 6 months beyond arrival
required_documents: Thai business invitation or meeting letter (recommended)
merged_guidance.onward_travel_evidence: Confirmed return or onward ticket within 60 days of arrival.
merged_guidance.accommodation_evidence: Proof of accommodation for the stay, such as a hotel booking or invitation/host letter.
merged_guidance.financial_evidence: Evidence of funds, e.g., 10,000 THB per person or 20,000 THB per family (cash, bank statement or equivalent).
exceptions: The exemption covers business contacts but not residing, employment, study or media activities
Cumulative visa-free stays under the bilateral agreement are capped at 90 days in any 180-day period

uncertainty.reason: China and Thailand have a bilateral 30-day visa-exemption agreement (with a 90-day-in-180-days cumulative cap) in addition to Thailand's unilateral 60-day exemption for Chinese nationals; the actual stamp and cumulative limit may depend on which rule the officer applies.

Visa exemption covers short-term business meetings and negotiations only; gainful employment, assignment, or long-term business requires a Non-Immigrant B visa and possibly a work permit, which the provided facts do not rule out.
I do not have a reliably current official Thai MFA or Immigration Bureau URL for this route; verify with the Thai embassy/consulate or official Thai eVisa portal before traveling.
